events.text: Late in the night {npc} wakes you, not for anything, only to say your name and hear you answer. You lie awake after. Whatever is between you is past wearing out now.

mem.note: said my name back in the dark

effects.log: You say it into the dark. {npc} is asleep again before you finish, smiling.

choices.text: Promise {him} the rest of your life

mem.note: promised me the rest of our years

effects.log: "The rest of it," you say. "Every year I have." {npc} holds you to it with both hands.

events.text: {npc} mends the sleeve you tore in a fight and says nothing about the blood on it. Then {he} says, quietly, "If you ever do not come home, I will come and find you." {He} means it.

choices.text: Tell {him} you will always come home

effects.log: {npc} ties off the thread with {his} teeth. "See that you do."

mem.note: showed me the roads and the inns

effects.log: You show {npc} the roads you take and the inns you trust. {He} learns every one by heart.

events.text: {npc} catches your sleeve in the courtyard and holds on a moment too long. "Whatever you become," {he} says, "come back here." The words settle in you like a stone at the bottom of a river.

effects.log: You promise. {npc} lets go of your sleeve, and keeps the promise instead.

choices.text: Hold on until {he} laughs at you

mem.note: held on longer than I did

effects.log: You hold on until {npc} laughs and calls you a child. Neither of you lets go first.

events.text: A fever takes you for three days. Each time you wake, {npc} is there, the same cup of broth in {his} hands, cold by now. On the third morning you understand that {he} never left.

effects.log: It is terrible. You drink all of it. {npc} pretends not to cry.

mem.note: sent me to sleep when I was worn out

effects.log: "Sleep," you say. {npc} sleeps in the chair by your bed, one hand still on the blanket.

events.text: {npc} kneels at dawn without being asked and pours your tea with both hands. "Master, if you fall, I will carry you down the mountain." Disciples say such things. This one meant it.

choices.text: Tell {him} to carry {his} own sword first

mem.note: told me to carry my own sword first

effects.log: {npc} grins and trains twice as hard. You catch {him} carrying stones up the steps for practice.

mem.note: poured tea for me before the hall

effects.log: A master pours for a disciple. The whole hall stops to stare. {npc} drinks it like a vow.

events.text: You find {npc} asleep against your door, sword across {his} knees. A rumour of assassins kept {him} there all night. There were no assassins. {He} would have stood there anyway.

mem.note: carried me in out of the cold

effects.log: {npc} wakes on your mat with your coat over {him} and goes red to the ears.

mem.note: stood a night of watch for me

effects.log: You stand the next night outside {his} door. {npc} hears of it, and never forgets it.

events.text: {npc} turns up at your door in the rain with two jars of wine and no reason. You drink until the jars are empty and the rain stops. Somewhere in the night the two of you became something the years will not undo.

choices.text: Cut your palms and swear it

mem.note: swore it in blood with me

effects.log: Two cuts, one handshake, a little blood on the table. {npc} laughs at the mess and does not let go.
There is a third jar after all. Neither of you remembers the end of the night. Both of you remember the rest.

events.text: On a bad road you turn and {npc} is already at your back, blade out, as if {he} had been there all along. Afterwards {he} only says, "Where else would I be?" You find you have no answer.

effects.log: "Always," says {npc}, wiping the blade, and somehow it sounds like a fact.
{npc} turns the knife over twice and wears it from that day on.

events.text: {npc} needed you and you were somewhere else. {He} does not say so. {He} sets out two bowls at supper, as always, and eats from neither.

choices.text: Say you are sorry, and mean it

effects.log: It is not easy to say. {npc} listens to all of it, and the thing between you holds, mended.
You let it pass. So does {npc}, or {he} seems to. The bond holds, thinner than it was.

events.text: You hear later that {npc} sent for you, and waited at the gate until dark. When you come, {he} smiles and talks about the weather. That is worse.

events.text: {npc} asked for you when {he} was in trouble, and you did not come. {He} still bows to you every morning, a little lower than before, as if to someone far away.

events.text: {npc} does not shout. {He} moves {his} bedding to the far room and sits down with {his} back to you. "I would have followed you anywhere," {he} says to the wall. "I will stay. Do not ask me for more."

effects.log: {npc} hears every word, and says nothing. {He} is still there, and far away. Some things do not mend; now you know which.
You let it be. {npc} stays in your life at a distance you cannot cross. The silence is very loud.

events.text: {npc} looks at you across the table as if counting the years back to someone {he} used to know. "I kept a place for you," {he} says. "I do not know who sits in it now."

events.text: {npc} still bows to you at morning practice, exactly as low as the rule asks and not a hair lower. "You taught me what a master is," {he} says once. "I will not forget the lesson."

events.text: {npc} hears you out to the end. Then {he} empties {his} cup onto the ground between you, slowly, as one does for the dead.

events.text: Word goes round that you gave a gift to everyone you know. An old woman at the well asks whether you are dying, courting, or both.

effects.log: You laugh. She does not believe a word of it, and tells the whole street so.

choices.text: Say it was a good year

effects.log: "A good year," you say. By evening it is a story about a fortune found in a well.

events.text: By the market's reckoning you handed out silver like a lord at a festival. Two strangers now claim to be your cousins, and one of them even has your nose.

effects.log: You press a few coins into each hand. The one with your nose bows very low.
You send them off. The one with your nose shouts that you will be sorry. You are not.

events.text: Your people talk of nothing but the pills you gave out. A physician from the next town calls, very politely, to ask where you buy them.

effects.log: He writes it all down and leaves with shining eyes. The herb seller has a rival now.
You pour him tea and say nothing at all. He goes away with a great deal to think about.
